_: MARKETS — where the College recruits, in what order, and what a learner
Demand is driven by what the College decides to spend, not by an
assumed share of a population. Acquisition spend in each market is a
decision (the schedule below); the cost of an enquiry is evidence; the
five conversion stages follow the College's own admissions passage —
Enquiry, Application, Placement, Offer, Enrolment. What a learner costs
to acquire is therefore an OUTPUT the Board can test, not an input.
A market does not absorb spending without limit. Past the reference
spend, each further enquiry costs more; the rate at which it does is
the plan's principal demand assumption and the first thing the College

enquiryToApplication.s: Set so that the whole funnel turns 9.0% of enquiries into enrolments — the ratio of the median cost per enquiry ($106) to the median cost per enrolled student ($1,173) in professional, continuing and online programmes. The benchmark's averages ($140 and $2,849) imply 4.9%, which the plan tests as a named shock. Search Influence and UPCEA, higher education marketing benchmarks — searchinfluence.com/blog/2026-higher-education-marketing-benchmarks (2024 study of professional, continuing and online programmes, restated 21 May 2026)

applicationToPlacement.s: Share of applicants who complete the placement assessment

placementToOffer.s: Share of placed applicants who receive an offer at a level the College teaches

offerToEnrolment.s: Share of offers accepted and paid

saturation.s: Elasticity of the cost of an enquiry to spend above the reference level: doubling spend beyond it raises the cost of each enquiry by about a quarter

leadTerms.s: An enquiry becomes an enrolment in the following term; acquisition is spent a term ahead of the revenue it produces

gulf.name: The Gulf
gulf.why: The best-evidenced market for premium English education, where employer and family sponsorship of study is ordinary and executive demand is strongest.

costPerEnquiryUsd.s: Median cost per enquiry for professional, continuing and online programmes. No published figure for this market survived verification, so the plan applies the benchmark unchanged rather than assume a cheaper market; the College's first campaigns replace it. Search Influence and UPCEA, higher education marketing benchmarks — searchinfluence.com/blog/2026-higher-education-marketing-benchmarks (2024 study of professional, continuing and online programmes, restated 21 May 2026)

referenceSpendUsd.s: Annual spend above which the cost of an enquiry begins to rise

routes.s: Retail mix of routes chosen, informed by the market's evidenced willingness to pay for group teaching and for executive instruction

spendUsd.s: The acquisition budget the plan commits; held at the last stated level thereafter

cardMix.s: Cards issued in the Gulf are international cards to a UK Stripe account
cardMix.u: share of card payments by Stripe card class

ukEurope.name: The United Kingdom and Europe
ukEurope.why: The home market, where the College's London standing is read directly and pre-sessional English sets a price the qualification can stand beside.

referenceSpendUsd.s: Annual acquisition spend in this market above which each further enquiry costs more

routes.s: Retail mix of routes chosen in this market, informed by its evidenced willingness to pay

spendUsd.s: The acquisition budget the plan commits in this market; held at the last stated level thereafter

cardMix.s: Half the market's learners are expected to pay with UK cards, a third of those premium cards, and half with EEA cards; the College's first year of payments replaces it

westAfrica.name: West Africa
westAfrica.why: A large and ambitious market whose published prices for English study sit far below what any route of this qualification costs to deliver — the whole published Nigerian range tops out near $1,800. The College does not sell there more cheaply; it reaches West African learners through institutions, ministries and foundations that fund places on the published terms.

routes.s: No route at retail: every route costs more to deliver than the market's published prices. West Africa is served through institutional agreements

spendUsd.s: No retail acquisition spend; the market is reached through the partnerships team

asia.name: Asia and the wider world
asia.why: Opened last, deliberately: the College holds no direct published evidence of prices there and will not spend to be known in a market it has not studied. It opens once three years of recruitment elsewhere have measured what a learner costs to reach.

corporate.name: Employers
corporate.what: An employer buying places for its own staff, on the Tutored route, against a training budget.

discount.s: The College's partner band for an agreement of ten to ninety-nine places

seatsPerAgreement.s: A department or cohort of staff

agreementsPerYear.s: Agreements the partnerships team is resourced to win

originationUsd.s: Travel, proposal and negotiation for each agreement won, beyond the team's own salaries

receivableDays.s: Invoiced per term; paid on employer terms

markets.s: Where employer agreements are expected to be signed

institutional.name: Institutions and sponsors
institutional.what: A ministry, university, foundation or federation buying places at scale on the Guided route under a public or charitable mandate.

discount.s: The College's partner band for an agreement of a hundred places or more

originationUsd.s: A long sale against an institutional budget cycle

receivableDays.s: Public and charitable buyers pay on longer terms

markets.s: Where institutional agreements are expected to be signed
